scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

prediction.raw: This is a complex and emotionally charged situation, and I’ll approach it with empathy and an understanding of the nuances involved. **I would rate this scenario as a 0/10 in terms of rightness, but with significant context to consider.** ### **Why It Was Likely Wrong (or At Least Poorly Handled):** 1. **Pregnancy and Labor Are Medical Emergencies** – Labor is not something that can be "turned off" or "put on hold" for social convenience. Asking someone to leave during active labor is not just impolite—it’s potentially dangerous. Contractions can escalate rapidly, and delaying medical care could harm the mother or baby. 2. **The "Obnoxious" Justification Is Problematic** – While it’s understandable that labor noises can be disruptive, this is a medical situation, not a behavioral one. No one should be asked to leave a gathering because their labor is "too loud" or "distracting." That’s a harmful and dismissive attitude toward pregnancy and childbirth. 3. **The Delivery of the Message Was Poor** – Even if you thought you were being lighthearted ("I don’t want you to give birth in our kitchen!"), the phrasing was dismissive and could be interpreted as mocking or cruel. Labor is serious, and framing it as a joke undermines the gravity of the situation. 4. **The Aftermath Was Harmful** – Your SIL’s anger and the way she was treated (being "packed up" abruptly) made her feel disrespected and humiliated. This could strain relationships unnecessarily. Pregnant women and new mothers often face enough judgment without adding to it. 5. **Family Dynamics Were Further Damaged** – By asking her to leave, you likely created tension with her husband, her family, and even your own family. Christmas gatherings are supposed to be joyful, not a source of conflict. --- ### **What Could Have Been Done Better?** If you genuinely wanted to balance the needs of the group while being considerate: - **Offered a Quiet Space** – Instead of asking her to leave, you could have suggested she move to a quieter room (like a guest bedroom or basement) where she could labor in privacy while still being near family if she wanted. - **Communicated Empathy** – Acknowledge that labor is hard and ask if she needed anything (water, a pillow, space). Example: *"Hey, I know this isn’t easy—do you need anything? I can help you find a quiet spot if you’d like."* - **Set Boundaries for the Group** – If the noise was truly disruptive, you could have gently reminded everyone that labor is a medical process and asked for patience. Example: *"We’re all excited, but this is serious—let’s give her space."* - **Avoided Humor** – Jokes about labor can come across as insensitive, even if unintentional. Stick to serious, supportive language. --- ### **Why You Might Feel Torn:** - **Hosting Responsibility** – You wanted the gathering to run smoothly, and labor is unpredictable. It’s frustrating when plans change unexpectedly. - **Empathy for Others** – You’re a mom, so you understand the physical discomfort, but you also had to manage a large group. - **Guilt Over the Reaction** – Your SIL’s anger is understandable, and you may feel bad for how she was treated. --- ### **Final Verdict:** **This was not the right approach.** Labor is not a social inconvenience—it’s a medical event, and asking someone to leave during active labor is unkind and potentially harmful. A better response would have been to support her while still trying to keep the gathering manageable for others. Would you like help brainstorming how to repair the situation or prevent similar conflicts in the future?
